dialogues.text_a: Can you operate a hydraulic car lift?
dialogues.text_b: No, I can’t. But I can use a tyre changing machine.
Of course, he can. He services petrol engines every day. He’s a trainee mechanic.

dialogues.text_a: When are you going to adjust the wheel alignment?
dialogues.text_b: I’m going to adjust it tomorrow morning.

dialogues.text_a: When is Ravi going to replace the brake pads?
dialogues.text_b: He might replace them this morning, or he might replace them this afternoon. He really doesn’t know.
Sunil is not feeling very well. He has back pain.
dialogues.text_c: Back pain? How did he get it?
dialogues.text_d: He lifted a heavy gearbox all day yesterday.

dialogues.text_a: Did you clean the engine parts properly yesterday afternoon?
dialogues.text_b: No, I didn’t. I was feeling too exhausted.

dialogues.text_a: Why did you tighten the wheel nuts again this morning?
dialogues.text_b: I tightened them again to make sure they were secure.

dialogues.text_a: I bought a new pair of safety gloves yesterday.
dialogues.text_b: Really? But I liked your old gloves. They were thick.
dialogues.text_c: That’s true. But my new gloves are thicker.

dialogues.text_a: Why are you checking the engine oil level right now?
dialogues.text_b: I’m checking the engine oil now because I checked it yesterday, but I made a mistake. I am going to service my uncle’s car this evening, and I might use this vehicle.
I am upset because I have to redo the brake inspection. I always tighten the bolts properly, but this morning I forgot, and it was a careless mistake.
I’m charging a car battery manually.
dialogues.text_c: That’s unusual. Do you usually charge batteries manually?
dialogues.text_d: No, I usually use a battery charger, but I am charging the battery manually today.
dialogues.text_f: Because the battery charger is not working.

dialogues.text_a: Can you and Amal test the vehicle lights now?
dialogues.text_b: No, we can’t. We have to finish changing the engine oil first.

activity_a.text:
Match the words to their definitions.
පදයන් ඔවුන්ගේ අර්ථයන්ට ගැලපෙන්න.
சொற்களை அவற்றின் வரையறைகளுடன் பொருத்துங்கள்.
to adjust a tool or machine so it measures or works accurately.
to put a part or component into position so it can operate correctly.
to find the cause of a mechanical or electrical problem.
to check a system step by step to identify and fix faults.
to position parts so they are straight, level, and working in the correct orientation.
to turn or spin a part around a central point.
to apply oil or grease to reduce friction between moving parts.
to increase the speed of a vehicle.
to remove air from a system, such as brake lines, so the fluid can flow properly.

Listen to the audio which will be played twice and click on the correct answer. It is very important that you read the questions before you listen to the recording.
ඔබට සෑම පටිගත කිරීමක්ම දෙවරක් ඇසෙනු ඇත. නිවැරදි පිළිතුර ක්ලික් කරන්න. රෙකෝඩින් එක අහන්නට පෙර ප්‍රශ්නය කියවීම ඉතාමත් වැදගත්ය.
ஒவ்வொரு ஒலிப்பதிவையும் நீங்கள் இருமுறை கேட்கலாம். கேட்ட எண்களை குறித்து எழுதுங்கள். பதிவைக் கேட்பதற்கு முன் கேள்விகளைப் படிப்பது மிகவும் முக்கியம்.

Questions.question: What did Imran read about the night before the interview?
options: All the automobile companies in his town.

Questions.question: What type of work does the company specialise in?
Which tool did Imran say he has used during training?
What task did Imran complete last month?
How does Imran plan to learn about advanced diagnostic scanners?
Questions.answer: By reading about them on the Internet.
options: By watching special tutorials on the Internet.
By reading about them on the Internet.

activity_b.text: Good morning, Imran. Nice to meet you.
Please relax and take a seat.
How are you feeling today?
Good morning, madam.
How are you today?
Quite good. I’m looking forward to talking to you about my future in the automobile field.
Great.
Let’s begin with something basic.
Tell me, what do you know about our company?
Last night I read about your company on the Internet.
I learned that you specialise in hybrid-vehicle servicing and that you recently opened a new diagnostic centre.
I also liked the way you use modern scanning tools in your workshops.
I’m glad you checked it.
Now, before we discuss your skills, tell me—what do you like most in the automobile industry?
Honestly, madam, I like solving real mechanical problems.
When we inspect brakes, adjust engine timing, or replace filters, I can see improvement immediately.
I also enjoy working in a busy, hands-on environment.
That’s good to hear.
And what tasks are you good at?
I am good at basic engine checks and keeping the service bay organised.
During my training, I replaced spark plugs, cleaned throttle bodies, and assisted my instructor during full-service inspections.
And what technical skills do you have?
I know how to read simple wiring diagrams, check fluid levels, and use tools like torque wrenches, multimeters, and OBD scanners.
Last month, I carried out a brake-pad replacement during a workshop practical.
We sometimes use advanced diagnostic scanners.
Are you familiar with them?
I am not familiar with them yet, madam, but I can read about them on the Internet.
That’s how I learned more about hybrid-battery maintenance.
Excellent.
Finally, why should we select you?
Because I learn fast, I work carefully, and I am always ready to support the team.
Thank you, Imran. We’ll contact you soon.
